pairs.subject: agent-memory
pairs.evidence: src/app/api/org/loop/propose/route.ts:141 The lane-brief preview turns a failed read of the org's standard (procedural memory, playbooks, skills) into brief:null, the same value used for foundation lanes and empty batches, and BriefStrip drops null proposals, so the operator cannot tell 'the lane will get no memory because the read failed' from 'there is nothing to brief'.

techniques.evidence: src/app/api/org/loop/propose/route.ts:141 'Empty is not broken, and the difference must be visible' fails here: a read failure collapses into the same null as 'no brief'. The engine (loop-lane.ts:1215) repeats the same catch-to-null.

src/lib/db/lane-brief-read.ts:91 The per-section memory reader this route calls catches every error and returns an empty list. buildLaneBrief then tells the executing agent 'This organization has recorded no procedural memory for this repository.' (lane-brief.ts:263): a degraded read that reads as empty, not unavailable.
src/lib/db/lane-brief-read.ts:80 Memory candidates are scoped to the repo namespace before recall ranks them, so one repo's lessons do not brief another repo's lane.

src/lib/org/lane-brief.ts:273 The section cap that runs after recall's own 4,000-char budget (lane-brief-read.ts:28) writes an in-text omission notice and records trimmed in provenance, so the second cut is visible.

pairs.subject: agent-memory
pairs.evidence: src/lib/org/developer-view-load.ts:64 The local mentor's durable care state (kept/dropped moves, journal, profile) is read with a catch-to-null that the comment says 'reads as "nothing shared"', so an unreadable store renders as 'Moves kept 0 / none yet' (DeveloperCompanion.tsx:28), even though the same loader gives the contributor snapshot a distinct 'unreadable' state at line 82.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/org/developer-view-load.ts:64 A degraded read of the stored mentor share is shown as empty rather than unavailable. The sibling activity read at line 82 shows the correct posture ('unreadable').
src/lib/org/developer-view-load.ts:36 The care memory is filed and read under the server-resolved owner identity, never a caller-supplied one. There is no counterpart axis here.
